core_obligations: Source side: by the carried equation-restriction diagram the morphism s' is the base change of h : U' x_{g,U,t} R to U along g; by assumption (2) the property P is preserved under base change, and by assumption (1) h has P, so s' has P. Target side: the same diagram shows t' is isomorphic to s' as a morphism of schemes, and having property P is invariant under isomorphism, so t' has P. Conclusion: both s' and t' have property P.
proof_roadmap: Exhibit s' as the base change of h via the carried restriction diagram and conclude s' has P by assumptions (1) and (2) (proof lines 973-974).
Conclude t' has P from t' being isomorphic to s' as a morphism of schemes (proof line 975).
